name: In-play two-sided sports quoting (RN1 model)
mechanism: Rest bids on BOTH outcomes of every two-outcome sports market from kickoff to final whistle, one tick wide (the two bids sum to 0.99), 2-3 levels, fixed share size per league, re-quote within seconds, never sell: pairs redeem for $1 at resolution, merge only when cash runs short. Edge is the ~1.5 cent toll per pair paid by impatient in-game buyers, plus maker rebates and a refund of part of its own taker fees. Unpaired leftovers are the cost.
time_gap: None in the maker's favour; the maker is the slow side. Fast takers with fresher scores/odds pick it off (seconds in-game, minutes to hours pre-game).
claimed_results: 10 Aug-10 Nov 2026: 911,860 fills, 222.5M spent, +1.6M from fills (0.71% of spend) plus 935K of daily payments = 2.53M; pairs +2.1M, leftovers -486K; in-game quoting +1.13M, pre-game quoting -283K; lost on 39 of 92 days, worst drawdown 323K; capital 1.2-2.7M.
evidence: wallet_check RN1 (0x2005d16a...75ea), re-run 2026-11-27: shown P/L 15,090,230; fees charged 5,343,676, refunded 3,852,784 (paid 1.49M); rebates+rewards 2,302,007 (taker 620K / maker 1.31M / rewards 375K); kept 15,901,347 = 2.13% of $747M volume; rebates/rewards 14% of kept all-time. Monthly gross / rebates / NET kept / net without rebates: Jul 1.72M / 415K / 1.83M / 1.41M; Aug 1.31M / 288K / 1.35M / 1.06M; Sep 561K / 361K / 628K / 266K; Oct 918K / 267K / 1.03M / 758K; Nov (to the 27th) 217K / 212K / 329K / 117K. Gross as % of volume: Jul 1.68, Aug 1.93, Sep 0.65, Oct 1.38, Nov 0.42. Rebates were 58% of net in Sep and 64% in Nov. Maker tier 4 (15%), 30-day maker weighted volume 19.1M; taker tier Platinum (25% under the 20-Nov table). The tool's Aug-Nov rows are consistent with the article's 2.53M for 92 days.
requirements: About $2M working capital turning over every few hours, coverage of ~1,000 live markets a day, sub-10-second re-quoting, and at least $10M of 30-day maker weighted volume for the 15% maker rebate (docs; RN1 itself runs at 19.1M). A new account gets no rebate and no fee refund.
fee_sensitivity: Maker fills pay no fee. Its own takes pay the sports rate 0.05 (1.25 c at 0.50). Without payments the fills alone earned 0.71% of spend; 37% of the quarter's total came from payments a small account will not receive. The 'half of own taker fees back' was the Aug-Nov regime (tool: 620K taker rebate against 1.36M charged since May); at RN1's current taker tier the table gives 25%.
testability: Whole-market tape (trades?condition=) for a sample of live matches gives maker-side P&L per price band and the share lost to the busiest takers; a simulated one-tick quote cannot be validated without book history (no cancels on chain), so only an upper bound is testable.
red_flags: Margin is falling (net without rebates 117K in November on $51M volume). 50 informed takers take back a third of maker profit. Pre-game quoting loses. ITF tennis is the worst series. Not a small-capital strategy: nothing here is reachable with a few hundred euros and no rebate tier.
verification: CONFIRMED. Both articles re-downloaded; every headline number (fills, spend, 0.71%, 935K, pair and leftover P&L, the four job rows, 42,885 wallets, top-50 takers -504K, ITF -331K, 39 of 92 losing days, 323K drawdown) is in the text, and the wallet tool agrees in order of magnitude. Corrected: the tier-4 threshold is $10M, not 19M.

name: Pre-match de-vigged-odds bidding with hedge in thin esports books (polymm / b00k13)
mechanism: Scrape sportsbook odds, remove the margin to get a fair probability, post a limit bid one cent above best bid wherever fair minus bid is at least 7 points, in pre-match esports markets with 20-30 cent spreads. When one side fills, bid the other so both sides cost at most 0.93; unhedged fills remain directional. Edge is a wide spread nobody else is quoting.
time_gap: Sportsbook lines move on roster/news before thin Polymarket books: minutes. It only helps if your reference is fresher than the other bots'; with 10-30 minute old odds the gap works against you.
claimed_results: Jan-Mar 2026: 3,858 bets, $95.8K volume, +$4,973 from a ~$1K start; locked arbs +$8.3K, forced directional -$3.2K. Fill rate fell 37% (Jan) -> 15% -> 5% -> 1% (Apr). Other sports net -$509. A later note says the Rust rewrite made $650 in a month (July).
evidence: wallet_check b00k13 (0x1c5575dc...84ce), re-run 2026-11-27: shown 6,293; fees charged 357, refunded 71; rebates+rewards 50 (1% of kept); kept 6,058 = 4.2% of $144K volume. Monthly NET kept: Jan 2,295; Feb 2,086; Mar 466; Apr 115; May 0; Jun 17; Jul 617; Aug -106; Sep 285; Oct 192; Nov 91 (to the 27th), on $2.7-4.7K monthly volume since September. Jan-Apr gross 4,961 matches the claimed 4,973.
requirements: $300-1,000, one VPS, an odds source refreshed far faster than 5 minutes (he pays ~$3/day for 5-minute odds from 9 API sources), team-name matching between venues, fast cancel on line moves.
fee_sensitivity: All entries are maker bids: no fee. The esports/sports taker rate 0.05 only matters if the hedge is taken. The edge did not die from fees but from faster bots and stale odds.
testability: His analytics scripts run on any public wallet (code not run here). Forward test: poll gamma for esports markets with spread above 10 cents and volume, log the book and The Odds API / Pinnacle lines every minute, count how often a 7-point bid would have been hit before versus after a line move.
red_flags: Author himself says a clone 'will mostly donate to faster bots'. Income is now under $300 a month. AI-written code shipped three mapping bugs that bet the wrong team. All published numbers are from before the window (Jan-Jul 2026); no post on kacho.io after 2026-08-13.
verification: CONFIRMED. Three posts re-read: 3,858 bets, $95,830, +$4,973, +$8.3K / -$3,184 split, 2,555-match line-move table, fill-rate decay, -$509, $3/day odds and the 'donate to faster bots' line are all there; the wallet reproduces the totals. Credibility 5 is for the truth of the account, not for the edge, which is nearly gone.

name: Pre-game stale-quote taking on sportsbook line moves and team news
mechanism: Watch a sharp reference (sportsbook lines, lineups) for pre-match sports and esports; when the line jumps, take the resting Polymarket bids/asks that have not moved, hold to resolution or sell after the book catches up. This is the other side of the two verified makers' losses.
time_gap: Sportsbook line or team-sheet news arrives minutes (sometimes tens of minutes) before resting Polymarket quotes are pulled.
claimed_results: No one claims this strategy by name. Indirect: RN1's own pre-game takes earned +7.36% after fees (+243K), all of the profit inside the last hour before start; RN1's pre-game resting bids lost 283K in 92 days (227K from fills an hour or more before start); Kacho's 7-point bids turned negative after line moves.
evidence: Not tested by anyone in the lab. Supporting measurement from Kacho: lines moved 5+ points before going live in about a third of 2,555 esports matches (CoD 60%, LoL 49%, Dota 2 37%, CS2 31%, Valorant 12%), sampled every 7-8 minutes, 6-20 Mar 2026. RN1 wallet figures as in the first candidate.
requirements: Live odds feed (Pinnacle or The Odds API paid tier), name matching, taker execution within seconds to a minute; small capital is enough because the stale size is small.
fee_sensitivity: Sports/esports taker rate 0.05: at most 1.25 c per share at 0.50. A 5-point line move leaves about 3.75 c after the fee at even odds; a 2-point move leaves under 1 c before spread and does not survive.
testability: Take RN1's pre-game maker fills from the public tape (trades?user=RN1&taker_only=false minus the taker feed), mark each to the price 30 minutes later and at resolution, and group by the taker wallet: that shows who collects the 283K and how fast. Forward: poll odds and CLOB books by REST each minute for a week.
red_flags: Inferred from the victims' accounts, not from a winner's. The BlockJuice author calls the team-sheet explanation 'my guess, still a guess'. The stale size on offer may be tiny. RN1 itself is a pre-game taker and may be the one collecting it. Kacho's line-move data is March 2026.
verification: PARTIAL. The supporting numbers are in the sources (-283K, 227K of it an hour or more before start, +7.36% / +243K, the line-move table). The figure '4,374 fills over 1,984 markets' was not found in the text of either article. The strategy itself is the researcher's inference; no source describes or claims it.

name: In-play score-feed latency taking
mechanism: Subscribe to a fast score/event feed, and when a goal, break of serve or map win lands, hit the resting quotes on Polymarket before makers re-quote; hold or sell into the stream-watching crowd.
time_gap: Official data feeds are claimed to lead TV/streams by 45-60 s and public APIs by 3-15 s; makers like RN1 re-quote within seconds (filled orders were a median 11.8 s old), so the usable gap is seconds.

The earlier note 'about 58K down in Jan-Apr' ignored the refunds and is withdrawn. The promoter does not lose, and does not show the edge he describes.

fee_sensitivity: Sports taker rate 0.05; in-game prices move 10-50 points on a goal, so the fee is small relative to a real event, but RN1's measured taker edge was only 1.36% after a fee that averaged 1.63% of what it paid.

The only source that names the strategy and a wallet is an advert, and that wallet keeps 0.12% of volume before rebates. Free feeds (ESPN ~10 s) are slower than the makers. Lowered from 3 to 2 for these reasons.

name: Breaking-news reaction on headline markets
mechanism: Monitor primary sources (press wires, company releases, official accounts) for an event that settles an open market, and buy the winning side while the book is still repricing; hold to resolution.
time_gap: Measured on one event in two markets: the book moved in the same minute as the stock (first aggressive prints 13:55:53 UTC), the first three wallets took everything under 0.30 within about 10 seconds, and the price passed 0.90 after 66-74 seconds. A reader 20-70 s behind bought at 0.50-0.85. A public hint 10 hours earlier (Trump's post) moved the price only from 0.08 to 0.11.

The article's release time (08:30 EST) is wrong by 25 minutes per the stock tape, so its timeline cannot be used as a trigger clock. mechanism: Mirror the buys of wallets with large all-time profit (or a high skill score) shortly after their fills appear.
time_gap: Negative: the follower is hundreds of milliseconds to minutes behind the leader, and the book moves on the leader's fill.

name: Near-certain 'bond' buying and settlement-lag discount
mechanism: Two variants that should be kept apart: (1) buy the side of an event that is already decided but not yet resolved, at 0.95-0.99, and wait for resolution; (2) buy the 'almost surely' side of an event that is still open (NO at 0.90-0.96 on unlikely things) and collect the discount. The return is the discount.
time_gap: Variant 1: event known, market unresolved: hours (UMA window) to months (the Ethiopia market stayed open 123 days after the election). Variant 2 has no time gap; it is selling insurance.

sources.author: Luke Garrison (summarising Reddit u/marvmarv2693)
sources.kind: news summary of a Reddit thread

claimed_results: Reddit backtest: settlement-lag discounts listed among ten ideas that failed (fee model unknown). Paper: the discount is a maturity-dependent price of locked capital; adjusting for it removes 48-88% of the apparent mispricing.
evidence: A named wallet found in the Huang tape: Tigerofthehood (0x9c261746...74bc), 267 markets, 19,689 fills, $38.9M volume, kept 270,051 = 0.69% of volume, rebates+rewards 4% of kept. Monthly NET kept: Dec-25 11,101; Jan 23,464; Feb -26,930; Mar 54,193; Apr 9,399; May 64,828; Jun 115,281; Jul -44,006; Aug 33,110; Sep 42,384; Oct 39,368; Nov -52,140. It bought NO on 'Huang rejoins' at 0.90 (15,620 shares, Dec-31 market) and 0.958 (35,000 shares, Nov-30 market) as a taker on 16-17 November and dumped 68,991 and 66,465 NO at 0.003-0.032 at 13:57 on the 23rd: about -46K on the visible part, about -120K if the rest of the position cost the same. Lab's earlier tape: buying at 0.90-1.00 in BTC 5m was the only positive taker bucket (+0.41 c per share after fees, not significant).
requirements: Capital that can sit locked; careful reading of resolution rules; diversification across many small positions. At 0.69% of volume the verified wallet needed $39M of turnover to keep $270K; a few hundred euros earns cents.
fee_sensitivity: Fee at p=0.97 is 0.15 c at rate 0.05 and 0.03 c at 0.01; zero on geopolitics. The fee is not the problem; the tail (a surprise, a dispute, a rule reading) and the lock-up are.
testability: data-api resolutions + prices-history (30-minute buckets kept 90 days): for markets that traded above 0.95 before resolution, compute realised return, days locked, and the frequency of reversals by category, separately for 'already decided' and 'still open'. Deconstruct Tigerofthehood's 267 markets to see which variant it runs and what the three losing months were.
red_flags: One surprise wiped out roughly five average months of the verified bond wallet. Search summaries (not opened) report over 1,150 UMA disputes in 2026 and a 0.99 market overturned by vote. Volume in dead markets is largely wash trading per Wired ($284M of $285M in the Ethiopia market), so displayed liquidity is not real. The Reddit result is second-hand.
verification: CONFIRMED for the sources: the arXiv abstract (48-88%), Wired (123 days, $284M between paired accounts, 38,000 loops, over 98% with no gain or loss, 99.6% flagged in the Romania market) and the Action Network line on settlement-lag discounts are as quoted. New wallet evidence added by this pass.

name: Own pricing model in new or niche markets, taking badly priced resting orders
mechanism: Pick market types the big firms do not model (newly invented formats, low-liquidity niches), spend weeks building a better way to price them, and take resting liquidity that sits at poor prices.
time_gap: None in the latency sense; the gap is in modelling effort.
claimed_results: qoez: 'you can easily come in and price it with a large edge'; says much of his money probably comes from SIG's own quotes. PredictPnL: the top 20 by skill have 1,962-17,960 closed trades, median all-time profit $469K, median result 0.7% of volume.
evidence: None; the commenter gives no account.
requirements: Domain model per market family, patience, small capital is fine because the stale size is small.
fee_sensitivity: Mentions, culture, economics, weather are at 0.01 (0.25 c at 0.50): the cheapest categories for a taker.
testability: Category leaderboards (data-api leaderboard?category=mentions|culture|weather) to find wallets with thousands of trades and low rebate share, then deconstruct entries.
red_flags: Anonymous, no numbers, no wallet. The PredictPnL figures describe skilled wallets in general, not this approach.
verification: CONFIRMED that the comment and the article say this; the claim itself is unverifiable.

name: Polymarket-Kalshi cross-venue arbitrage and hedged quoting
mechanism: Match the same event on two venues, buy YES on one and NO on the other when the sum is under $1 after fees, or quote on one venue and hedge fills on the other.
time_gap: One venue reprices before the other: seconds.

sources.author: Luke Garrison (summarising Reddit comments)
sources.kind: news summary of a Reddit thread

claimed_results: peikail: $3-4K a day net for two weeks on Kalshi + Polymarket US, no losing day, record 'under NDA'. Reddit commenter: 233 screens a day with zero executions under strict thresholds. NBA paper: 7 executable single-market arbs in 173 games (median life 3.6 s), 290 combinatorial episodes.
evidence: None measured.
requirements: Accounts and capital on both venues. The one profit claim is on Kalshi and Polymarket US, which is a separate US venue from the Polymarket this lab studies; access for a Serbian resident not checked. Capital split and idle, automated matching of contract terms.
fee_sensitivity: Two taker fees: vendors put break-even near 3.5-4 cents per pair at even odds (search summary, not opened).
testability: Kalshi public market data and the Polymarket CLOB are both reachable here by REST: poll matched pairs and count seconds where the cross sum after both fees is under 1 and the size available.
red_flags: The only profit claim is two weeks long, unverifiable, from a job-seeker, and on a different venue. Settlement wording differs between venues. The paper and the Reddit commenter both point to near-zero executable size.
verification: CONFIRMED that the four sources say what is quoted (HN post, Show HN, Action Network line, arXiv abstract). No independent check of any result.

name: Fade longshots / base-rate NO
mechanism: Systematically sell (or avoid) cheap YES contracts on 'will X happen by date' markets, on the belief that longshots are overpriced and most such markets resolve NO.
time_gap: none

The source is a paid data product; its trading rules and sizing are not published.

name: Liquidity-reward farming (resting two-sided quotes near the midpoint)
mechanism: Keep two-sided limit orders close to the midpoint in markets with a daily reward pool. Score per order is ((v - s)/v)^2 times a market multiplier, where v is the market's maximum spread and s the distance from the midpoint; the two-sided score is the smaller of the two sides; one-sided quotes are divided by 3 and score zero when the midpoint is outside 0.10-0.90. Paid daily pro rata per market, with a $1 minimum that is not carried forward.
time_gap: none (the risk is the reverse: being filled at a stale price when news lands)
market_categories: any market with a reward pool

name: Cross-market logical arbitrage (nested sports lines, crypto threshold ladders, text-inferred relations)
mechanism: Prices of logically related contracts must sit inside the convex hull of admissible payoffs (over 3.5 goals implies over 2.5; spread cover implies moneyline win; 'BTC above 65,000' implies 'above 64,800'; partitions sum to 1). When fee-adjusted best quotes violate a relation, take every leg at once (buy the implied contract, sell or buy NO on the implying one) and hold to resolution or unwind. The edge is that relations the venue does not publish are slower to be enforced.
time_gap: Not an outside-information gap: the lag is between two Polymarket books. Median window 2.9 s for venue-published NegRisk relations, 6.3 s for relations rebuilt from sports metadata, about 31 s for relations inferred from resolution text: s

fee_sensitivity: Fee rate is 0 on these markets today (feeType zero_fees, confirmed on all 12 H100 December markets) although finance/tech is 0.05 in the fee table; if the holiday ends the fee at p=0.5 is 1.25 cents a share.
testability: Can start now, no waiting for December: (1) replay Kalshi's settled Sep and Oct ladders (daily candlesticks, already pulled once) against the Ornn history with a proper distribution for the remaining days instead of a range bound; (2) from 2026-12-01 record the Ornn settle and the Polymarket ladder books around 05:00 UTC every day and measure how long quotes stay unchanged after the new value appears.
red_flags: No settled Polymarket month yet. On the only venue with history the decided Yes side was already offered at 0.98-1.00 and the stale bids were 50 contracts. Polymarket's ladder has 1-cent spreads and paid market makers who can do the same arithmetic. The daily index is noisy (3% a day is normal), so strikes within about 10 cents of the running mean stay open until the last days. Ornn's free tier covers only three months and its terms were not read. The verifier's 'decided' dates used a crude range bound and should not be reused.
verification: PARTIAL. The settlement arithmetic is confirmed (rule text on the live event; Ornn's free daily history; Kalshi's two settled months equal the mean of the daily values). The claim that the book still prices doubt on decided strikes is not confirmed: Kalshi's history shows it only as small stale bids, and Polymarket has no history.

name: Polymarket vs Kalshi on the same H100 monthly-average strikes
mechanism: Both venues list 'average H100 price in <month> above $X'. Buy Yes on the venue where it is cheap and No on the other when the two cost under $1, or buy a lower strike on one venue against selling a higher strike on the other at the same price. Hold to settlement.
time_gap: none (price disagreement between venues; persists minutes to days in thin books)
claimed_results: None.
evidence: Re-pulled by the verifier a few hours after the researcher: Polymarket Yes above $3.50 (December) ask 0.11; Kalshi bid 0.17 for 50 contracts (was 0.18): 0.11 + 0.83 = 0.94 per $1 before a Kalshi taker fee of about 1 cent, i.e. roughly $2.50 of profit on $50 locked for five weeks. The second gap (Polymarket above $3.20 at 0.38 vs Kalshi above $3.25 bid) is gone: Kalshi's bid is now 0.35. Kalshi December quotes are 50-lots with 30-60 cent spreads, open interest 27-1,523 contracts. Rules: Kalshi says 'arithmetic mean of hourly values reported by Ornn', Polymarket says mean of finalized daily settled values; in practice Kalshi's Sep and Oct settled at 2.83 and 2.94, equal to the mean of Ornn's daily values (2 of 2).
requirements: Accounts on both venues (Kalshi availability from Serbia not checked), capital locked on both sides until month end, manual execution is fine.
fee_sensitivity: Polymarket leg 0 fee today; Kalshi taker fee 0.07*p*(1-p), about 1 cent at 0.17. A 6-cent gap survives it, on 50 contracts.
testability: Poll both ladders hourly for a month, record gaps with sizes on both sides, and compare the two settlement values for November and December.
red_flags: Capacity is tens of dollars: one maker's 50-contract quotes. Rule texts differ (hourly vs daily mean) even though two months matched. One of the two reported gaps disappeared within hours. Kalshi may not be open to the owner.
verification: PARTIAL. Both books re-pulled: one gap exists at 50 contracts, the other is gone. Rule equivalence is not in the texts but held for the two settled months.

name: Compute perp against the prediction-market ladder
mechanism: Polymarket's H100-USD perpetual (live since 2026-11-26) tracks the 24-hour average of Ornn hourly prints; the prediction ladder prices the distribution of next month's average of the same index. Trade the ladder against a perp hedge when the ladder's implied median and the perp disagree, or use the perp to hedge inventory picked up while farming rewards in the ladder.
time_gap: none by itself; the perp and the index move hourly, the ladder is repriced by hand
claimed_results: None.
evidence: Verifier's pull (evening of 2026-11-27): H100-USD index 3.1569, mark 3.157, mid 3.127 (1.0% under the index), open interest 12,952 GPU-hours (about $41K), 24 longs and 15 shorts; B200 and B300 have one long and one short each. December ladder implied median about $3.05. That is not a discrepancy by itself: Ornn's monthly means were 2.83, 2.94 and 3.15 in Sep-Nov while daily values ranged 2.46-3.53, so a December mean 10 cents under today's index is ordinary.
requirements: A perps account with separate margin, $10 minimum notional, a model for a monthly average of a noisy index.
fee_sensitivity: Perp taker 0.05% and maker 0.02% of notional at the entry tier, plus hourly funding; ladder fee 0 today.
testability: Record perp mid, index and the ladder daily through December and January; test whether the perp's level predicts the settled monthly average better than the ladder's implied median.
red_flags: Product is one day old; perp open interest is about $41K; a binary on a monthly average is not hedged by a linear perp except near the money; the reported 'gap' is within the index's normal month-to-month movement.
verification: PARTIAL. Index definition confirmed in the docs page and the tickers re-pulled; nothing about a tradable relationship has been tested.

name: Sports post-game settlement discount (resting bids at 0.99+ before on-chain resolution)
mechanism: After a game is decided, holders sell the winning token at 0.99-0.999 to free capital instead of waiting about 15-20 minutes for resolution. The only leg that exists after the game is the RESTING BID at 0.99-0.999, redeemed at $1 on resolution. Lifting offers at 0.99+ is something else: it happens in the closing minutes of play and carries in-play risk.
time_gap: The result is known from the broadcast/score feed; on-chain resolution follows 16-19 minutes after the last play on NBA games (15-minute challenge window on sports). Lag scale: minutes.
claimed_results: None from a source; measured only.
evidence:
239 sports/esports game markets resolved 11-27 Nov 2026, none disputed (237 at the 0.05 fee, 2 at 0.03). The researcher's headline reproduces from the saved fills: taker buys at 0.99-1 within 2 h of resolution $4.44M, net +0.227%.

Verifier's split by minutes before resolution. Taker BUYS at 0.99+: none in the last 15 minutes (the post-proposal window); 15-30 min: 125 markets, $2.44M, net +0.285%, no losing market; 30-60 min: 132 markets, $1.73M, +0.476%, one $16 loss; 1-2 h: 13 markets, $0.27M, -1.88% (Eagles-Cowboys, takers paid 0.99+ for the eventual loser 90 minutes before resolution, -$6.7K). Resting bids filled at 0.99+ (taker sells): last 15 min 232 markets, $5.32M, +0.101%, no loser; 15-30 min 236 markets, $9.23M, +0.144%, no loser; 30-60 min $2.52M, +0.210%; 1-2 h $0.16M, -0.49% (the same game). All: $17.36M, +0.135%, about $23K for every maker together in nine days.

Below 0.99 there is no taker edge: all taker buys at 0.90+ in the last 24 h lost 2.81% pooled ($27.0M), and in 32 of 239 games takers bought the eventual loser at 0.90+.
requirements: A score feed to know the game is over, capital that turns over several times a day, queue position at 0.999 (price-time priority, 0.001 tick) against whoever already collects this flow.
fee_sensitivity: A resting bid pays nothing. For a taker the sports rate 0.05 costs 0.05 cents per share at 0.99, about a fifth of the gross.
testability: For each resolved game take the final-whistle time from the ESPN API, then from the full tape (no row cap) measure volume and prices between final whistle and resolved_at, who the buying makers are, and how long capital stays locked.
red_flags: A tenth of a percent per turn: $200 earns about 20-30 cents per complete turn if it is first in the queue. The taker version is in-play betting at 0.99, and its one loss wiped out a quarter of the two-hour bucket. 84 of the 239 tapes hit the script's 3,000-row cap, so all 24-hour totals are lower bounds from the end of the tape. Nine days of data, no dispute or voided game in the sample.
verification: PARTIAL. The measured numbers reproduce from the saved fills, but the mechanism as written does not: nobody buys the winner at 0.99+ as a taker after the game, that flow is end-of-game betting. Only the resting-bid leg is real, at 0.10-0.14% per turn.

name: Buying the proposed outcome during the UMA challenge window (non-sports)
mechanism: Once a resolution is proposed on UMA the market settles after the challenge window unless disputed. Buy the proposed outcome below $1 (or rest bids) during that window; the risk is a dispute (4-6 days locked, possible reversal or 50/50).
time_gap: The event has happened and a proposal is on-chain; the price can still trade under $1 for the challenge window: 2 hours by default, 15 minutes on daily-temperature and sports markets, 10 minutes on crypto level markets (gamma customLiveness, per NOTES.md); days if disputed.
claimed_results: None.
evidence: Not measured by the researcher (the sample collapsed to 23 markets, 20 of them one event). Evidence already in the lab that the researcher did not use: in mentions markets, blindly buying the first print at 0.95+ is negative after the fee on the later half of the sample, with 4.2% of Yes confirmations and 1.6% of No confirmations resolving the other way (1,382 markets, 29 Sep - 23 Nov); economics bucket markets resolve about 2 h after the number and 98.8% of the stale money was taken within 60 s. The sports data in this catalog shows that after a proposal there are no offers to lift, only bids being hit.
requirements: A way to find markets in the proposed state (the /v2/resolutions endpoint takes condition or event ids only, there is no status listing), reading the rules of each market, patience for disputed cases.
fee_sensitivity: 0.01 rate categories cost 0.01 cents per share at 0.99; 0.05 categories 0.05 cents; a resting bid pays nothing.
testability: Page closed markets with the keyset endpoint by close time, take proposal times from /v2/resolutions (or UMA logs), and compute fills available between proposal and settlement, including every disputed market.
red_flags: Untested here; the losses sit in the disputed tail, which a short sample misses; the lab's mentions result argues against the blind version; the default 2-hour window does not apply to the fastest categories.
verification: PARTIAL. The lifecycle (2-hour default window, 4-6 days if disputed, 50/50 outcome) is in the live docs page; there is no measurement, and existing lab data on mentions points the other way.

name: Proposing resolutions on UMA for the proposer reward
mechanism: Post the bond with the correct outcome as soon as a market can be resolved; if nobody disputes within the challenge window the bond comes back with a reward.
time_gap: none (a service fee for being first to report a known outcome)
claimed_results: None; the docs do not state the reward size.
evidence: Not measured; reward sizes and who proposes were not pulled. The docs say the bond is 'typically $750 pUSD'; gamma fields read earlier by the lab show $250 on sports games and daily-temperature markets, $500 by default and $25-50K on the largest politics markets.
requirements: $250-750 per concurrent proposal, precise reading of rules, speed against established proposers.
fee_sensitivity: No trading fee; the cost is the bond at risk.
testability: Read proposer addresses, rewards and dispute outcomes from the UMA oracle contracts for Polymarket questions over three months.
red_flags: The smallest bond seen is about the owner's whole stake; one wrong or early proposal loses it all; no reward size is known, so there is no evidence of any income.
verification: PARTIAL. The bond-and-reward mechanism is in the live docs page; the bond size differs from what the lab read in gamma, and nothing about the reward exists in any source opened.

name: Rebate-tier economics (strategies that only pay with volume rebates)
mechanism: Above $200K of 30-day weighted volume a taker gets 10-60% of fees back and a maker 3-15% of the taker fees its fills generated. High-frequency books (BTC 5-minute and similar) are run at about break-even before rebates and live on the rebate.
time_gap: ms to s (speed race)
claimed_results: n/a
evidence: wallet_check on needleladder: November volume $1,013,690 in 28,268 fills, 30-day weighted volume 91,168 (taker) and 125,531 (maker), tier 0 on both, rebate 0 bps; all-time gross -43,273, fees -5,115, rebates 1,807 (taker 209, maker 1,598), rewards 47,591, kept 1,010. Oct -12,764 gross / -2,139 net; Nov -27,522 gross / +6,034 net. pootythetemperaturefarmer maker weighted volume 20,668, tier 0. Of the 12 wallets checked only xtxpleasecallme has a taker tier (Gold, 648,965). Since 2026-11-20 Gold/Platinum/Diamond pay 10/25/40% and daily maker pools were replaced by tiers (changelog).
requirements: Several hundred thousand dollars of monthly turnover before the first tier; co-location for the fast markets.
fee_sensitivity: Entirely: without the tier the same trades pay the full 0.01-0.05 rate.
testability: POST gamma /tiers and /v1/maker-tier/tiers for any wallet; compare economic P&L with and without rebates in wallet_check.
red_flags: Not reachable with a small stake; any strategy copied from a rebate-tier account does not transfer. The docs add that a maker rebate campaign can replace the standard rate, which nobody has looked for.
verification: CONFIRMED. Tier tables and the Nov 20 change are in the live docs and changelog; needleladder's tier 0 with $1.01M of November volume matches the tool to the dollar.

name: Holding rewards (4% a year on positions in eligible markets)
mechanism: Positions in markets flagged holdingRewardsEnabled earn 4.00% annualised on position value, sampled hourly, paid daily. Uses: park capital in a long-dated near-certain position there, or prefer these markets when quoting so that inventory earns while it waits.
time_gap: none
claimed_results: 4.00% annualised, variable (docs).
evidence: Re-pulled: 73 open events carry the earn-4 tag, $174.9M of liquidity, 32 of them Ornn events; all 12 H100 December markets have holdingRewardsEnabled = true. On $200 the reward is $8 a year. Whether a Yes+No pair from a split counts at full value was not verified.
requirements: None beyond holding.
fee_sensitivity: One entry fee can exceed a year of the reward (0.05 rate at p=0.5 is 2.5% of notional); only makes sense with a maker entry or a zero-fee market.
testability: Needs an account to see the daily credit; from outside only yield_income in user-stats of holders.
red_flags: Rate is at Polymarket's discretion; immaterial at this stake.
verification: CONFIRMED. The 4.00% sentence is in the live docs page and the event count and flag were re-pulled from gamma.

name: Negative-risk complete-set and conversion arbitrage
mechanism: In a negative-risk event one No of outcome A converts into one Yes of every other outcome. If the Yes asks of all outcomes sum below $1, buy them all; if the Yes bids sum above $1, buy a No, convert and sell the Yes tokens.
time_gap: none (internal consistency of one event); windows last seconds
claimed_results: n/a
evidence: The lab's earlier snapshot (NOTES.md, 2026-11-27): 176 open negative-risk events, none with a complete-set arbitrage after fees; median sum of asks 1.036, sum of bids 0.965; sums below 1 were all augmented events with an unnamed 'Other'. Not repeated by the researcher or the verifier.
requirements: Fast multi-leg execution, capital for every leg, the conversion call through the relayer.
fee_sensitivity: A taker fee on every leg (0.01-0.05 rate times p(1-p)); with many legs it eats a 1-3 cent gap.
testability: Poll all negative-risk events every few seconds for a week and count how long any gap beyond fees survives.
red_flags: Sums under 1 in augmented events are not arbitrage (the placeholder outcome can win); bots already keep the sums inside the fee band; profile P&L of accounts that use conversions is unreliable (NOTES.md).
verification: PARTIAL. The conversion rule and the augmented-event warning are in the live docs page; the only measurement is the lab's earlier single snapshot, which found nothing.

name: Combos (parlays) through the RFQ auction
mechanism: A user requests a price for a multi-leg combo; connected market makers have 400 ms to quote, the user 10 s to accept, and a maker with Last Look has 1 s to decline. The maker's edge is pricing correlated legs and the last look; a requester could in principle accept only quotes below the product of the legs' executable prices.
time_gap: A maker with Last Look sees up to about 11 s of new information before committing; the requester gets none.
claimed_results: None.
evidence: Docs only. Combos pay the 0.05 fee rate and earn no maker rebate; Last Look is offered to makers with about $2,500 of combo notional.
requirements: Maker side: a persistent RFQ WebSocket, a correlation model, capital locked until every leg resolves. Requester side: an account and the RFQ API.
fee_sensitivity: 0.05 rate on the combo price regardless of the legs' own categories.
testability: Only indirectly from public data: /v2/positions/combos and realized_combo_pnl in user-stats of wallets that quote; the quote stream itself needs an account.
red_flags: Structure favours the maker (last look); no public record of quotes.
verification: PARTIAL. 400 ms, 10 s, the $2,500 Last Look threshold and the 0.05 combo fee are in the live docs pages; the 1-second Last Look length was not found by a text search of the two pages.

name: Maker quoting behind the sports taker delay
mechanism: On sports markets around live play a marketable order is held for the market's configured delay and cannot be cancelled, while resting orders can be cancelled at any time. A maker with a fast score feed can pull quotes inside that window, so in-play takers are structurally late.
time_gap: Score events reach a fast feed seconds before a delayed taker order matches. The delay is 1 second on NFL, college football and basketball, NHL, soccer, tennis and most esports, and 0 on NBA (gamma secondsDelay, per NOTES.md).
claimed_results: None.
evidence: In 239 games takers who bought at 0.90+ in the last 24h lost 2.81% of $27.0M after fees, and resting bids at 0.90+ gained 0.50% on $20.2M of taker sells (lower bounds: 84 tapes were cut at 3,000 rows). The larger dollar-weighted gain at 0.90-0.95 (+5.7%) is a duration effect: by market count 8.6% of games had loser fills against about 7.5% implied. These are in-play aggregates across delayed and non-delayed leagues, not a test of the delay.
requirements: A low-latency score feed, automated cancel logic, inventory across many games.
fee_sensitivity: Maker pays nothing; the taker on the other side pays the 0.05 rate, which widens what a maker can earn.
testability: The delay values are already known: compare maker markout before and after game start on the tape for 1-second leagues against NBA (0 seconds), which is a natural control.
red_flags: Competing makers already do this; the numbers do not isolate the delay; the researcher says the delay length was not pulled although NOTES.md had it; the same notes file quotes a 50 ms crypto delay that has been 150 ms since 2026-09-04.
verification: PARTIAL. The rule (pending marketable orders cannot be cancelled, resting ones can) is in the live docs page; the aggregate numbers come from the saved fills; the delay's own effect is untested.

name: Referral and builder-fee income (why 'bot made $X' posts carry links)
mechanism: Not trading. A referrer earns 10% of a new user's net fees for 30 days (5% for second-level referrals). A builder who routes other people's orders can add up to 1.00% of notional on taker orders and 0.50% on maker orders, plus weekly volume rewards once verified. Both pay the promoter whether or not the promoted strategy works.
time_gap: none
claimed_results: n/a
evidence: Docs only. A user routed through a third-party terminal at the 1% builder cap pays 1% of notional on top of a taker fee that is at most 1.25% at p=0.5. Referral income is visible per wallet: ArmageddonRewardsBilly shows 11,256 of yield plus referral income.
requirements: Referrer needs $10,000 of lifetime volume; a builder needs users.
fee_sensitivity: For us it is a cost to avoid: never trade through a third-party front end that attaches a builder code.
testability: referral_income in user-stats of any promoter's wallet; builder leaderboard and volume endpoints of the Data API.
red_flags: Self-referral and linked accounts are clawed back. The docs rate (10% / 5%) disagrees with the lab's X sweep, which recorded affiliates earning 20%+ of referred fees since 2026-10-23; the two were not reconciled.
verification: CONFIRMED. 10% / 5%, the $10,000 threshold, the 30-day and Platinum limits and the 100 bps / 50 bps builder caps are in the live docs pages.

name: Perps liquidity rewards and trading competitions
mechanism: Daily pUSD pools per perp market ($325 or $100; ANT $3,000 until 2026-11-30) shared by score of two-sided depth near the mid; competitions rank by PnL times the square root of boosted volume.
time_gap: none
claimed_results: n/a
evidence: Docs only: a firm must hold at least 1% of its tier's maker volume over 7 days and quote $1,000-5,000 per side within 10 bps to score at all.
requirements: Tens of thousands of dollars of margin and a professional quoting system.
fee_sensitivity: Maker fee 0.02% of notional at the entry tier is paid on every fill while farming.
testability: Perps public book and trades endpoints; not pursued.
red_flags: Closed to a small account by the eligibility rule.
verification: CONFIRMED. Pool sizes ($325 / $100 / ANT $3,000 through Nov 30), the 1% eligibility rule and the score formula are in the live docs pages; nothing was measured.

name: Kalshi x Polymarket two-leg arbitrage (buy YES on one venue, NO on the other for under $1)
mechanism: Hand-match the same event on both venues, buy YES where it is cheap and NO on the other when the two asks plus both taker fees sum below $1, hold both to settlement. The edge is supposed to be a price gap between venues with separate order books and separate customers.
time_gap: none (a level gap, not a timing gap). Published gross gaps close in about a minute on liquid books; the gaps that survive fees are long-dated and simply sit there (15 of 16 unchanged between my two snapshots 39 minutes apart).

name: Kalshi as a leading quote for Polymarket sports (in-play follow)
mechanism: Watch Kalshi's book for the same game; when Kalshi reprices and Polymarket has not, take the stale Polymarket quote (or, as a maker, pull or move resting quotes). The edge is supposed to be Kalshi's larger sports flow moving first.
time_gap: about 1 s or less on quotes (ZenHodl 1-second NBA data: both venues reprice within about 1 s); 7 s median only on trade prints (Pantera), which Polymarket's block-time stamps and taker delay inflate; nothing visible at one minute (researcher's check)

The Binance-minus-index basis measured by the script was +73 in the first run and +89 in the second. name: News-headline sniping on deadline ladders (hit stale resting orders in the first seconds after a headline)

Edge: resting 'bond' bids (No at 97c), wide asks and reward-farming quotes whose owners do not react for 5-70 s, so the book stays at pre-news prices while the fact is already public. (Correction: the exchange's cancel latency is not the main cause; cancel p50 is 24 ms and p95 78 ms, only p99 is 0.6-0.7 s.)
time_gap: Headline on newswire/X before the Polymarket book. Source figures on two events: first serious buyer +3-5 s, 50c after ~24 s, 95c after 72 s (Nov 23); 35c to 97c in 33 s (Nov 12). The lab's own tape of Nov 23 agrees: first aggressive print 13:55:53 UTC, 0.90 reached after 66-74 s. Sister deadline lag about 3 s. Scale: seconds.

name: Tennis walkover: markets resolve 50-50 when a player withdraws before the start (alive, not historical)
mechanism: Rule in the market text: 'If the match ends in a walkover (player withdraws before the start and the other advances automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50' (a retirement after the start resolves to the player who advances). Observed: Paris Masters 2026-11-03, favourite still printing 0.74 at 09:33 UTC, underdog taken at 0.28 from 09:38, scheduled start 11:30, market closed at 0.5/0.5 at 12:30; Metz 2026-11-18, underdog taken at 0.32 at 11:15:58, closed 11:56. time_gap: Station observation vs book: the book reprices within ~1-2 min of the observation time stamp, which is 3-5 min BEFORE the official source (aviationweather.gov, NOAA tgftp) shows the report. name: Tweet-count markets: count on X directly, ahead of the official tracker
mechanism: Elon post-count events resolve on the 'Post Counter' at xtracker.polymarket.com. Count qualifying posts on X in real time and trade the bucket boundaries in the last hours before the noon-ET deadline.
time_gap: X feed vs tracker: measured in the lab's culture study at a median 161 s (p10 35 s, p90 296 s, p99 5,807 s) over 1,294 posts. Whether the book follows X or the tracker has not been measured.

name: Mention markets: hear the word before the stream viewers do
mechanism: Markets resolve Yes if the speaker says a listed term during a named event (source: audio/video of the event). Use the lowest-latency stream plus speech-to-text, buy Yes the moment the term is said; or sell remaining No value as the event ends.
time_gap: Room or low-latency stream vs standard streams: 5-40 s (assumed, no source); speech-to-text 1-3 s. On Polymarket the first print after the word is already >=0.90 in 57% of 131 clean live jumps (lab mentions study).

name: Election night: trade raw vote counts ahead of network calls
mechanism: Model county-level results as they post and buy the race/chamber before the market reaches 99c; the public 'call' is not a signal because the market is hours ahead of it.
time_gap: Market vs network calls: market 1-2.5 hours AHEAD (Kalshi House contract 99% at 8:10pm vs NBC 10:08pm; Senate 9pm vs 11:26pm; Polymarket about an hour ahead of CNN on the Texas governor race). Count feed vs book: minutes, unmeasured.

name: Off-chain fill vs on-chain settlement gap ('ghost fills') - a risk, not a strategy
mechanism: A fill reported by the API is provisional until the on-chain transaction succeeds; an attacker makes his own order fail on-chain (for example by moving the balance before settlement) after the match has removed maker liquidity or after a bot has hedged against it.
time_gap: Match vs chain: 2-3 s.
